types.EditOp: { op: 'add'; feature: Record<string, unknown>; index?: number }
types.EdgeRule: { parallel?: 'X' | 'Y' | 'Z'; outside?: [Vec, Vec]; inside?: [Vec, Vec]; not?: EdgeSel; onFace?: FaceSel; lengthGreater?: number; lengthLess?: number; near?: Vec; within?: number; union?: EdgeSel[]; intersect?: EdgeSel[]; difference?: EdgeSel[]; }
types.SketchSpec: { on: 'front' | 'top' | 'right' | at(plane, offset) | face(sel); draw?: (s) => void; point?: [x, y]; name?: string }

methods.summary: A standard plane moved along its normal, for a sketch on a workplane at a distance.
methods.description: at(plane, offset) returns a plane reference for sketch(): front moves along +Z, top along +Y, right along +X. A reference plane feature is added to the part. Use it to sketch above or below the origin without needing a face to select.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description: the standard plane: front, top or right

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: distance along the plane normal in mm (a number or expr)

methods.signature: .sketch(plane: Plane | OffsetPlane | FaceSel, build: (s: SketchBuilder) => void, name?: string): this
methods.summary: Start a sketch on a plane or a face; the next extrude, cut or revolve uses it.
methods.description: Opens a sketch on 'front' (XY, normal +Z), 'top' (XZ, normal +Y), 'right' (ZY, normal +X), on at('front', 20) (a plane moved along its normal), or on a face(): face('>Z'). The callback draws with the sketch builder `s`. A feature needs its own sketch: each extrude / cut / revolve consumes the last sketch. Units mm, Y is up.

parameters.name: build
parameters.description: callback receiving the sketch builder s

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: optional name shown in the feature tree

methods.notes:
- A sketch on a face(): the sketch origin is the world origin projected on that face; coordinates are in mm.
- Feature order matters: sketch, then the feature that uses it. Two sketches in a row without a feature between them: only the last is used.
- Units mm, Y up. front = XY (normal +Z), top = XZ (normal +Y), right = ZY (normal +X).

methods.signature: .sketchFeature(on: Plane | OffsetPlane | FaceSel, json: { points: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; entities: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; constraints?: Array<Record<string, unknown>> })
methods.summary: Append a raw sketch (points, entities, constraints) on a plane.
methods.description: For sketches the builder cannot draw: pass the kernel's sketch JSON { points, entities, constraints? } and the plane ('front' | 'top' | 'right', at(plane, offset) or face(sel)). The next extrude, cut, revolve or rib consumes it. Point ids and entity ids are yours; remember the origin point O exists only if you declare it.

parameters.name: json
parameters.type: { points: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; entities: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; constraints?: Array<Record<string, unknown>> }
parameters.description: { points: [{ id, x, y }], entities: [{ id, type, ... }], constraints?: [] }

methods.example:
part('Tri').sketchFeature('front', { points: [{ id: 'a', x: 0, y: 0 }, { id: 'b', x: 20, y: 0 }, { id: 'c', x: 0, y: 20 }],
  entities: [{ id: 'e1', type: 'line', p1: 'a', p2: 'b' }, { id: 'e2', type: 'line', p1: 'b', p2: 'c' }, { id: 'e3', type: 'line', p1: 'c', p2: 'a' }] }).extrude(5);

methods.signature: s.arc(centre: Pt, start: Pt, end: Pt): this
methods.summary: Counter-clockwise arc about a centre from a start point to an end point.
methods.description: Adds an arc on the circle through `start` centred on `centre`, running counter-clockwise to `end` (projected on the radius). For an arc through three points in either direction use arc3.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: [x, y] where it ends (counter-clockwise from start)

methods.signature: s.arc3(a: Pt, m: Pt, b: Pt): this
methods.summary: Arc from a to b passing through the middle point m (either direction).
methods.description: Adds the arc of the circle through the three points. It fails if the points are in line. Easier than arc() when you know three points on the outline.

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: a point on the arc between a and b

methods.summary: Construction line along the sketch Y axis (the default revolve axis).
methods.description: revolve() adds this automatically when the sketch has no axis, so you rarely call it. Profile x is the distance from the axis, profile y the height along it.

methods.summary: Construction line used as the revolve axis when it is not the sketch Y axis.
methods.description: Adds a construction line between two sketch points and makes it the axis of the next revolve. Normally you pass the same thing as revolve(360, { axis: { from, to } }), which calls this for you.

methods.summary: Circle given its RADIUS (not diameter).
methods.description: Adds a circle of radius r centred on `at`. Remember radius: a 10 mm bore is circle(5). Several circles in one sketch with nesting make rings; a circle on a face with cut() makes a round pocket or a through bore.
methods.notes:
- RADIUS, not diameter: a 10 mm bore is circle(5).
- To drill, prefer part.hole / holes.* over a circle + cut: they carry the hole kind and are one feature.

methods.signature: s.cvspline(pts: Pt[], o: { closed?: boolean; degree?: number } = {})
methods.summary: Control-vertex spline: the points are the control polygon, not on the curve.
methods.description: Adds a B-spline whose control vertices are the points (the curve is pulled towards them but does not pass through). Degree 3 by default. Use it for fair, smooth outlines where overshoot of an interpolating spline is a problem. closed: true makes a periodic loop.

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: control points [x, y], at least degree + 1

properties.name: closed
properties.description: close the curve into a loop

methods.signature: s.grid(origin: Pt, pitch: Pt, count: [number, number]): this
methods.summary: Points on a rectangular grid.
methods.description: Adds nx by ny points starting at `origin` with spacing `pitch` along x then y (x varies fastest).

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: [nx, ny] number of points along x and y

methods.summary: One line segment between two points.
methods.description: Adds a single line from a to b. Combine with arc or arc3 to close a profile that has curved sides (a half disc is arc3 plus a line).

methods.summary: A single point (a hole centre).
methods.description: Adds a point entity. Points in a sketch are used as hole centres by hole features; for a hole use part.hole or part.holes.* rather than placing points yourself.

methods.summary: Several points (hole centres).
methods.description: Adds one point entity per [x, y]. See holes.points for the usual way to drill them.

methods.signature: s.polarPoints(center: Pt, radius: number, n: number, startAngle: number = 0): this
methods.summary: Points on a circle: a bolt circle of centres.
methods.description: Adds `n` points on a circle of `radius` about `center`, the first at `startAngle` degrees (counter-clockwise from sketch x). For drilled holes use part.holes.polar.

methods.summary: Closed polygon through the points.
methods.description: Adds a closed profile of straight lines through the points, in order; the last point joins the first. Coordinates are in the sketch plane in mm. Use it for L, T, U shapes and for revolve profiles (half cross-section).

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: list of [x, y] points, at least three

methods.notes:
- Points go in order around the profile, either direction; the shape closes itself.
- For a revolve profile keep every x >= 0 (radius).

methods.summary: Open chain of lines through the points.
methods.description: Adds line segments joining consecutive points without closing. An open chain extrudes only when thin walls are requested (thin option) or when it is closed by other entities of the same sketch.

methods.signature: s.rect(w: Num, h: Num, at: Pt = [0, 0]): this
methods.summary: Rectangle of width x height centred on a point.
methods.description: Adds a closed rectangle: width along sketch x, height along sketch y, centred on `at` (default the sketch origin). A second rect inside the first makes a frame (ring) that extrudes as a hollow section.

methods.signature: s.rrect(w: Num, h: Num, r: Num, at: Pt = [0, 0]): this
methods.summary: Rounded rectangle: width x height with corner radius r.
methods.description: Adds four lines and four arcs that share end points, centred on `at`. With r <= 0 it is a plain rect. Prefer this over filleting the vertical edges of a plate afterwards: it is faster and more robust.

methods.summary: Interpolating spline: a smooth curve through the points.
methods.description: Adds a spline that passes through every point (a fit-point spline). closed: true makes it a closed loop through the points (a profile you can extrude); open splines are paths for sweep or lofts guides, or edges of an outline with other entities.

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: list of [x, y] points the curve passes through, at least 3 (2 for an open one)

properties.name: closed
properties.description: close the curve into a loop

methods.summary: Bevel edges with an equal distance.
methods.description: Cuts a flat bevel on the chosen edges, the same distance along both faces. Good for edge breaks on bores and rims.

methods.summary: Cut the last sketch out of the body: a depth or through().
methods.description: Removes material. The cut runs AGAINST the sketch normal: from a face sketch (face('>Z')) that is into the body; from a standard plane whose normal points into the body (the front plane at the start of a Z extrude) it runs away from the body and reports cutNoEffect, so sketch on a face or pass flip: true. Depth is a number or through() for all the way. Same options as extrude (mid, flip, draft, thin).
methods.notes:
- A cut runs AGAINST the sketch normal. On face('>Z') that is into the body. On the front plane at z = 0 with the body above it, it runs away: the run reports `cutNoEffect`; sketch on the face instead, or pass `{ flip: true }`.
- A cut sketch must overlap the material in plan; a circle outside the body also gives `cutNoEffect`.
- Several shapes in ONE sketch are ONE cut feature (draw pockets in a loop, then cut once).
- Depth beyond the body is fine; through() is clearer when you mean all the way.

methods.summary: Extrude the last sketch into a solid (adds material).
methods.description: Extrudes the last sketch along its plane normal by `depth` mm. Options: mid (symmetric about the plane), flip (opposite direction), draft (taper angle in degrees), thin (hollow wall thickness: closed profile gives a tube, open profile a thin sheet). The first extrude makes the body; later ones add to it (a boss when sketched on a face).

properties.name: thin
properties.description: wall thickness for a thin-walled extrude

methods.notes:
- Each extrude consumes the sketch before it: sketch again for the next feature.
- A sketch on a face adds material outward (a boss). On the 'front' plane it goes +Z, on 'top' +Y, on 'right' +X; flip reverses, mid is symmetric.
- On the 'top' and 'right' planes the sketch axes are not x/y of the world: when an offset position matters, sketch on a face or check with a probe.
- Nested closed shapes in one sketch (rect inside rect) give a ring, not two solids.
- draft is in degrees and tapers the sides inward for a positive angle on a boss.

methods.summary: Append any kernel feature as raw JSON (escape hatch for features without a helper).
methods.description: Validates json.type against the kernel's feature list, assigns the id and adds the feature after the previous step. face(sel) inside the JSON becomes the persistent face name (or a { kind: 'face', id } reference under plane / neutral / axis), edges(sel) becomes the edge references (spliced into arrays), at(plane, offset) becomes a reference plane feature, and the strings '$last' and '$sketch' stand for the id of the previous feature / sketch. Use it for types like draft, helix, lip, dome or moveFace; prefer the typed helpers when one exists. Field names are the kernel's (docs/spec-agent-interface.md).

parameters.name: json
parameters.description: the feature object, e.g. { type: 'shell', faces: [face('>Z')], thickness: 2 }

methods.summary: Round edges with a constant radius.
methods.description: Rounds the edges chosen by edges() with a fillet of the given radius (mm). Fails when the radius is too big for the adjacent faces (blendOverflow): reduce it. Fillet before shelling and before adding small features; select with edges('|Z') for the vertical edges of a block.
methods.notes:
- A radius that is too big for the neighbouring faces gives `blendOverflow`: halve it. Radius equal to half a face width is already a limit.
- Fillet before shell and before small holes; fillet edges('|Z') for the vertical edges of a block, or draw sketch.rrect instead.
- A fillet selected by edges() of faces that do not exist yet fails with a Line N selector error: select at the point in the chain where the edge exists.

methods.signature: .gear(o: { module: number; teeth: number; thickness: number; bore?: number; pressureAngle?: number; type?: 'spur' | 'helical' | 'internal'; helixAngle?: number; plane?: Plane; center?: [number, number] })
methods.summary: Involute spur or helical gear (profile, body extrude, bore) from module and teeth.
methods.description: Adds the app's gear generator output: a profile sketch with true involute teeth, the body extrude and a through bore. The gear is centred on `center` on the 'front' plane (axis +Z) unless plane says otherwise. Pitch diameter = module * teeth; outside diameter = module * (teeth + 2). Use it as the first feature of a part (it makes the body), or on its own plane for a second gear.

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { module: number; teeth: number; thickness: number; bore?: number; pressureAngle?: number; type?: 'spur' | 'helical' | 'internal'; helixAngle?: number; plane?: Plane; center?: [number, number] }

properties.name: bore
properties.description: bore diameter in mm, 0 for none, default 8

properties.name: helixAngle
properties.description: helix angle in degrees for a helical gear, default 15

properties.name: plane
properties.description: 'front' (default) | 'top' | 'right' or at(plane, offset) (offset planes are not supported: use a standard plane)

properties.name: center
properties.description: [x, y] of the gear centre in the plane, default [0, 0]

methods.signature: .loft(sections: SketchSpec[], o: { ends?: { first?: End; last?: End }; guides?: SketchSpec[]; centre?: SketchSpec; startNormal?: boolean | Num; endNormal?: boolean | Num; op?: 'add' | 'cut' } = {})
methods.summary: Loft a solid through two or more section sketches, optionally ending in a point.
methods.description: Builds one sketch per section (on a standard plane, an at(plane, offset) plane or a face) and a loft feature through them in order. Sections are { on, draw } where draw(s) draws a closed outline with the sketch builder, or { on, point: [x, y] } for a single-point section. Only the FIRST and the LAST section may be a point (a bow, a cone tip); ends.first / ends.last say 'cap' (flat end, default) or 'point' and are checked against the sections. Optional guides are sketches the loft follows, centre is a straight centre-line sketch, startNormal / endNormal (true or a tension number) make the loft leave the end sections along their normals. Closed (ring) lofts are not supported by the kernel. Section outlines should have the same number of pieces and be simple closed curves; a hull is a row of arcs or polygons with growing size.

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: list of section sketches, at least two, in order

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { ends?: { first?: End; last?: End }; guides?: SketchSpec[]; centre?: SketchSpec; startNormal?: boolean | Num; endNormal?: boolean | Num; op?: 'add' | 'cut' }

properties.name: guides
properties.description: guide curve sketches ({ on, draw }) that touch every section

properties.name: centre
properties.description: centre-line sketch ({ on, draw }) with a straight line

properties.name: startNormal
properties.description: true or a tension: leave the first section along its normal

properties.name: endNormal
properties.description: true or a tension: arrive at the last section along its normal

methods.signature: .revolve(angle: Num = 360, o: { op?: 'add' | 'cut'; thin?: Num; axis?: { from: Pt; to: Pt } } = {}): this
methods.summary: Revolve the last sketch about an axis (lathe parts: pulleys, bushings, flanges).
methods.description: Revolves the last sketch `angle` degrees (default 360). The axis is the sketch Y axis unless axis: { from, to } gives a line in the sketch plane. Profile x is the radius, y the height along the axis, so draw a half cross-section on one side of the axis. op: 'cut' removes the revolved volume instead. thin makes a revolved shell.

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { op?: 'add' | 'cut'; thin?: Num; axis?: { from: Pt; to: Pt } }

properties.name: thin
properties.description: wall thickness for a thin revolve

properties.name: axis
properties.description: { from: [x, y], to: [x, y] } axis line in the sketch plane

methods.notes:
- Draw the half profile on ONE side of the axis: x is the distance from the axis, y the height. Keep the profile from crossing the axis (no negative x).
- The sketch plane decides the world axis: on 'front' and 'right' the sketch Y axis is world Y or world Z accordingly; for a pulley on 'right' the axis is world Y and the end faces are face('>Y') / face('<Y').
- 360 is a full solid of revolution; a smaller angle leaves two planar end faces.

methods.summary: Rib: a web of a given thickness from an open sketch line, grown to the body.
methods.description: Takes the LAST sketch, which must be an open line or chain (not closed) lying across the body, and adds a rib of this thickness that extends from the line to the existing material. Use it for gussets and webs between a plate and a wall. flip reverses the growth side.

methods.summary: Hollow the body to a wall thickness, opening the selected face.
methods.description: Hollows out the solid leaving walls of `thickness` mm and removing the selected face to make an opening (box open at the top: shell(face('>Z'), 2)). Do fillets of the outside edges before the shell. A thickness larger than the smallest feature fails (shellTooThick).

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: face(sel) of the face left open

methods.notes:
- Fillet or chamfer the OUTSIDE edges before shelling; shelling a rounded box keeps even walls.
- The selected face is REMOVED (the opening). To close the box again sketch a lid on the rim face and extrude it (recipe hollow-box-lid).
- A thickness that is too big gives shellTooThick / shellFailed with maxThickness in the error.

methods.signature: .sweep(profile: SketchSpec, path: SketchSpec, o: { twist?: Num; op?: 'add' | 'cut' } = {})
methods.summary: Sweep a closed profile along a path sketch (pipes, rails, handles).
methods.description: Builds the profile sketch and the path sketch and sweeps the profile along the path. The profile must lie in a plane that the path starts on and is perpendicular to (a circle on 'front' for a path leaving the origin along +Z, which a path sketch on 'right' or 'top' draws as a line in its y or x direction). The path can be a line chain, arcs or a spline. twist turns the profile by that many degrees over the path; op 'cut' removes the swept volume. The kernel has no keep-normal option: the profile follows the path frame.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: path sketch { on, draw } (open chain starting on the profile plane)

properties.name: twist
properties.description: total twist in degrees over the path

methods.summary: Make the previous extrude or revolve a thin-walled one.
methods.description: Edits the step recorded just before it: the same as passing the thin option. Closed profile gives a hollow section of this wall thickness (centred on the profile).

methods.summary: End condition for cut(): through all material.
methods.description: through() is passed to cut() instead of a depth to cut all the way through the body, in the direction the cut goes (against the sketch normal).

methods.summary: Select edges of the current body by direction, extreme plane, or a rule object.
methods.description: edges(sel) is resolved against the body just before the step that uses it. Strings: 'all'; '|X' '|Y' '|Z' straight edges parallel to that axis; '>X' ... '<Z' edges lying in the extreme plane along that axis. A rule object ANDs its keys: parallel ('X'|'Y'|'Z'), outside / inside (box [[x0,y0,z0],[x1,y1,z1]] tested on the edge midpoint), not (another edges()), onFace (a face()), lengthGreater, lengthLess, near + within (radius), and union / intersect / difference (arrays of edges()). It fails with a line number when nothing matches.

parameters.name: sel
parameters.description: a selector string, or an EdgeRule object

methods.notes:
- Rule keys AND together; use union / intersect / difference for combinations.
- edges('>Z') selects edges lying in the highest plane only (after a boss, that is the boss rim). Combine with onFace or not to refine.
- A selector that matches nothing is an error with the script line, not a silent no-op.

methods.summary: Select one planar face of the current body by direction: >X <X >Y <Y >Z <Z.
methods.description: face(sel) is resolved when the script runs, against the body as it is just before the step that uses it. '>Z' is the planar face whose outward normal is +Z and which lies furthest along +Z (ties: the biggest face). '#top' is '>Z' and '#bottom' is '<Z'. Only planar faces match; it fails with a line number when none does. Pass it to sketch(), hole(), holes.*, shell().
methods.notes:
- Matches planar faces only, by outward normal direction; ties go to the biggest. It does not pick by position: two coplanar faces at the same height resolve to the larger.
- Resolved against the body as it is just before the step: after a boss on top, face('>Z') is the boss top, not the plate top.

methods.signature: .hole(on: FaceSel, at: Pt, o: HoleOpts): this
methods.summary: A simple drilled hole on a planar face at [x, y].
methods.description: Drills a round hole into the material from the face. kind selects the shape: 'simple' (default), 'cbore' (counterbore: cboreDiameter and cboreDepth), 'csk' (countersink: cskDiameter, cskAngle default 90) or 'tapped' (thread: 'M6' drills the tap drill and adds the thread; modeled: true for the real helix). size: 'M6' + fit instead of diameter uses the ISO table. end: 'upTo' drills to the next face. [x, y] are coordinates in the sketch plane of that face, measured from the part origin projected onto it (not from a corner). Through unless depth is given. Use flip: true if it cuts the wrong way on an unusual face. Diameter, not radius.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: face(sel) of the planar face to drill from

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: [x, y] hole centre in the face sketch plane

properties.name: depth
properties.description: blind depth in mm, omit for through

properties.name: thread
properties.type: string | boolean | { size?: string; length?: Num; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; modeled?: boolean; class?: string }

methods.notes:
- diameter, not radius (circle() is radius). Centres are in the face sketch plane relative to the world origin projected on the face, NOT a corner of the face: a hole at [0, 0] on a plate centred on the origin is in the middle.
- face('>Z') must exist as a planar face at that step. After a shell or fillet on the top, the top face may be a different face: select again.
- Through unless depth is given. Many holes: use holes.points / polar / grid (one feature).

methods.signature: .holes.grid(on: FaceSel, g: { origin: Pt; pitch: Pt; count: [number, number] }, o: HoleOpts): this
methods.summary: A rectangular grid of holes.
methods.description: Drills nx by ny holes from `origin` at `pitch` spacing, as one feature.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: face(sel) of the face to drill from

parameters.name: g
parameters.type: { origin: Pt; pitch: Pt; count: [number, number] }
parameters.description: { origin: [x, y], pitch: [dx, dy], count: [nx, ny] }

properties.name: thread
properties.type: string | boolean | { size?: string; length?: Num; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; modeled?: boolean; class?: string }

methods.example:
part('Perf').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(60, 40)).extrude(4)
  .holes.grid(face('>Z'), { origin: [-20, -10], pitch: [10, 10], count: [5, 3] }, { diameter: 4 });

methods.signature: .holes.points(on: FaceSel, pts: Pt[], o: HoleOpts): this
methods.summary: One hole feature at a list of centres.
methods.description: All holes share diameter and depth. Centres are [x, y] in the face sketch plane.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: face(sel) of the face to drill from

properties.name: thread
properties.type: string | boolean | { size?: string; length?: Num; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; modeled?: boolean; class?: string }

methods.signature: .holes.polar(on: FaceSel, c: { center: Pt; radius: number; count: number; startAngle?: number }, o: HoleOpts): this
methods.summary: A bolt circle: count holes equally spaced on a circle.
methods.description: Drills `count` holes on a circle of `radius` about `center` (sketch-plane coordinates, usually [0, 0]), the first at startAngle degrees. All holes are one feature.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: face(sel) of the face to drill from

parameters.name: c
parameters.type: { center: Pt; radius: number; count: number; startAngle?: number }
parameters.description: { center: [x, y], radius, count, startAngle? degrees }

properties.name: thread
properties.type: string | boolean | { size?: string; length?: Num; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; modeled?: boolean; class?: string }

methods.example:
part('Flange plate').sketch('front', (s) => s.circle(40)).extrude(8)
  .holes.polar(face('>Z'), { center: [0, 0], radius: 28, count: 6 }, { diameter: 6 });
methods.notes:
- One feature for the whole bolt circle. center is [x, y] in the face sketch plane (usually [0, 0] for a centred disc); startAngle shifts the first hole (degrees).
- Check that radius + diameter/2 stays inside the face and that holes do not overlap the centre bore.

methods.signature: .thread(on: string | undefined, o: { size?: string; diameter?: number; pitch?: number; length?: Num; standard?: string; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; modeled?: boolean })
methods.summary: Add a thread (cosmetic or modeled) to a hole or a cylindrical face.
methods.description: Threads the wall of the hole drilled last (default), or a cylinder named by a persistent face name ('F2.S.c1') or 'last:c1' (the c1 face of the last feature, e.g. an extruded circle shaft). Give the designation as size ('M6', 'M12x1.5', '1/4-20') or diameter (+ pitch). Cosmetic by default: no geometry change, the thread is reported in the regen threads list. modeled: true cuts the real helical groove (slow, falls back to cosmetic with a warning when it cannot). For a hole the hole diameter should be the tap drill of the size: use hole() with thread instead, which sets it.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: omitted or 'hole' for the last hole; a face name string; or 'last:<tag>'

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { size?: string; diameter?: number; pitch?: number; length?: Num; standard?: string; hand?: 'right' | 'left'; modeled?: boolean }

properties.name: diameter
properties.description: major diameter in mm (alternative to size)

properties.name: pitch
properties.description: pitch in mm with diameter (fine pitch)

properties.name: length
properties.description: thread length in mm, default the whole face

methods.signature: .circularPattern(o: { count: number; axis?: 'x' | 'y' | 'z'; angle?: number }): this
methods.summary: Repeat the last feature about a world axis.
methods.description: Repeats the last feature `count` times around the x, y or z axis over `angle` degrees (360 = equally spaced full circle). The axis passes through the world origin, so centre your part on it. For a ring of drilled holes holes.polar is simpler.
methods.notes:
- The axis passes through the world origin: centre the part on it, or the copies swing around the origin instead of the part.
- Repeats ONLY the last feature. For a ring of drilled holes use holes.polar (one feature, simpler).

methods.signature: .linearPattern(o: { count: number; spacing: Num; axis?: 'x' | 'y' | 'z' }): this
methods.summary: Repeat the last feature along a world axis.
methods.description: Repeats the feature added just before it `count` times (including the original) every `spacing` mm along the x, y or z axis. The seed is only the last feature: build the pocket or boss first, then pattern it.
methods.notes:
- Repeats ONLY the last feature (one seed), count includes the original, spacing is between instances in mm.
- axis is a WORLD axis ('x' | 'y' | 'z'), not a sketch axis.
- Patterning twice (rows then columns) is not supported by the helper: draw the whole grid in one sketch with a loop, or use holes.grid.

methods.signature: .mirror(plane: Plane | OffsetPlane | FaceSel, o: { body?: boolean } = {})
methods.summary: Mirror the last feature (or the whole body) about a plane.
methods.description: Adds a mirrored copy about 'front' | 'top' | 'right', at(plane, offset) or a planar face(sel). By default the feature added just before (a boss, pocket, hole) is mirrored; with body: true the whole body is reflected and united with the original. The kernel always keeps the original, there is no move-only mirror. Mirror about a face only when the face is the symmetry plane (a face you sketch on is usually not).

properties.name: body
properties.description: mirror the whole body instead of the last feature

methods.summary: Surface: sew all surfaces so far into one body (a solid when they close).
methods.description: Knits every surface feature made earlier in the script. With solid: true a closed set becomes a solid body (knitNotClosed when there are gaps); with solid: false (default) the result stays a sheet.

properties.name: solid
properties.description: make a solid from a closed shell

methods.example:
part('Box from sheets')
  .sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(20, 20)).surfaceExtrude(10)
  .sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(20, 20)).surfacePlanar()
  .sketch(at('front', 10), (s) => s.rect(20, 20)).surfacePlanar()
  .knit({ solid: true });

methods.summary: Surface: extrude the last sketch into a sheet (no end caps, not a solid).
methods.description: Like extrude but the result is a surface body (open sheet). Use thicken() to give it a wall, or knit() a closed set of sheets into a solid. A closed profile gives a tube sheet open at both ends; an open sketch gives a ribbon.

methods.summary: Surface: loft a sheet through section sketches (open or closed curves).
methods.description: Like loft() but the result is a surface body, so open curves (arcs, splines) work as sections. All sections should be the same kind (all open or all closed). Thicken it for a shell-like panel.

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: list of { on, draw } section sketches, at least two

methods.summary: Surface: a flat sheet filling the last closed sketch.
methods.description: Makes a planar surface body from a closed profile. Use it to cap surface tubes before knit(solid: true).

methods.summary: Surface: give the last surface a wall thickness and make it a solid.
methods.description: Thickens the most recent surface feature (surfaceExtrude, surfacePlanar, surfaceLoft or knit) into a solid wall of this thickness. It fails on a surface that folds or has a pole (thickenFailed).

methods.signature: .insertPart(doc: Record<string, unknown>, o: { at?: [number, number, number]; fixed?: boolean; name?: string } = {})
methods.summary: Assembly: insert another part (its document) as a component, optionally moved.
methods.description: Adds an insertPart feature that carries the whole part document (the .document of a runScript result, or a saved part). The component is its own body in the model, so a later mate() can position it. at moves it by [x, y, z] mm; fixed keeps mates from moving it. A part document is needed, not code: run the other script first. Assemblies live inside one part document; there is no separate assembly document in the script API.

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { at?: [number, number, number]; fixed?: boolean; name?: string }

properties.name: at
properties.description: [x, y, z] placement in mm, default [0, 0, 0]

methods.example:
const pin = { format: 'ck-part', version: 1, name: 'Pin', features: [], seq: 1, rollback: null };
part('Asm').insertPart(pin, { at: [10, 0, 0] });

methods.signature: .mate(o: { kind: string; a: FaceSel | string; b: FaceSel | string; distance?: Num; angle?: Num; flip?: boolean })
methods.summary: Assembly: constrain two faces of different components.
methods.description: Adds a mate of the given kind between faces a and b: coincident, parallel, perpendicular, concentric (round faces), distance (needs distance), angle (needs angle), tangent, lock. a and b are face(sel) of the current body or a persistent face name string ('F2.S.e1@F6.1' where @F6.1 names the inserted component). flip reverses the alignment. The component that is not fixed moves.

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { kind: string; a: FaceSel | string; b: FaceSel | string; distance?: Num; angle?: Num; flip?: boolean }

properties.name: a
properties.description: first face: face(sel) or persistent name

properties.name: b
properties.description: second face: face(sel) or persistent name

methods.example:
part('Stack').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(20, 20)).extrude(5)
  .mate({ kind: 'coincident', a: face('>Z'), b: face('<Z') });

methods.summary: A parameter written as an expression over the variables.
methods.description: expr('w/2') keeps the feature parameter linked to the variable w (stored as =w/2). Inside a sketch an expr contributes its current number only. Characters are limited to arithmetic and Math.*.
methods.example:
const { w } = variables({ w: 40 });
part('Bar').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(w, 10)).extrude(expr('w/4'));

methods.summary: Start the part the script builds; returns the fluent builder.
methods.description: Every script builds one part (the last wins). Chain sketch, extrude, cut, holes, fillet, ... on the result. The name appears as the document name.

methods.signature: variables(defs: Record<string, number | string>): Record<string, number>
methods.summary: Declare named values; strings are expressions over earlier ones.
methods.description: variables({ w: 60, t: 'w/10' }) defines document variables (editable in the Variables tab) and returns their numbers for use in the script. Use expr('w*2') to keep a feature parameter linked to a variable instead of a fixed number.
methods.example:
const { w, t } = variables({ w: 60, t: 'w/10' });
part('Bar').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(w, 10)).extrude(expr('t'));
